clue.text: Bit of clipper sailor's occupying?

indicators.note: a bit of the word clipper is its opening letter here

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor; 's reads as 'is'
occupying a place means being in it

explanation.surface: A question about which part of a fast sailing ship a seaman lives in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: C from the start of clipper, then AB (sailor) is IN, and the result is a sailor's room on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's cabin is a compartment a crew member occupies, a small part of the vessel.

clue.text: Explorer abandoning vehicle ahead of new group of fighters

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the vehicle's letters are dropped from the explorer

parts.note: Christopher Columbus, the explorer who crossed the Atlantic in 1492
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An explorer leaves his transport behind and goes ahead of a fresh band of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a formation of troops marching in file, a body of fighters.

clue.text: Book is rather lacking that certain something — that's a handicap

indicators.note: lacking means doing without, so the letters of the certain something are removed

parts.note: rather and quite both mean fairly
IT is that indefinable quality, charm or appeal

explanation.surface: A book without charm is presented as a handicap to its reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes IT from QUITE, leaving QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: In croquet and real tennis a bisque is an extra free turn or point granted as a handicap.

clue.text: Number — number reduced by 20% - gets comment on farm

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller; by 20% says how much, one letter of a five-letter number

parts.note: eight is a number, five letters long

explanation.surface: A statistician cuts a figure by a fifth and gets a remark down on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 20%' cuts one of the five letters of EIGHT, leaving EIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's whinny is the remark one farm animal makes, so it is a comment on a farm.

clue.text: American to stop daughter securing flat in US city

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the first pieces close round the flat

parts.note: in American slang to can something is to stop it
flat and level both mean even

explanation.surface: An American moves to stop his daughter getting an apartment in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts LEVEL inside CAND, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland is a large city in Ohio on Lake Erie.

clue.text: Theatricality fitting in good religious gathering

parts.note: camp is exaggerated, theatrical behaviour
fitting and meet both mean proper or suitable

explanation.surface: Theatrical showiness slipped into a pious gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp meeting is an open-air evangelical religious service, often lasting days, held in tents.

clue.text: I'll be taking no flights? Rising anger after heading out

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read from the bottom up
the head, or first letter, is taken out

parts.note: to fume is to seethe with anger

explanation.surface: Someone vowing never to fly again as their temper rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading out' leaves UME from FUME; 'Rising' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian bird is too heavy to fly, so it could say it will never take wing.

clue.text: Recording number of years controlling border line — it's not at all long

indicators.note: controlling here means the years take charge alongside the border, the two set together in the entry

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hem is the border of a garment
an era is a span of years

explanation.surface: A recording of a long period of years on a border line, which is then declared brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' tempts as part of the wordplay, but the definition is the whole closing phrase: something short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral lasts only a very short time, the opposite of enduring.

clue.text: Tasteful stuff from married relatives in excellent area

indicators.note: in places the married relatives inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as I
bros is short for brothers

explanation.surface: In-laws gathered in a fine area produce something with good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so anything delicious to eat.

clue.text: Get untidy to confound and upset most of distinguished party

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin or confound them

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the letters run bottom to top
most of drops the last letter

parts.note: a levee is a formal reception held by a monarch or dignitary

explanation.surface: Instructions for wrecking a smart party and making a mess of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims LEVEE to LEVE, and 'upset' turns it to EVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to make hair or clothes messy, causing them to get untidy.

clue.text: Hostile sumo wrestling in Scottish port

indicators.note: wrestling bodies tangle and twist, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An aggressive sumo bout staged in a harbour town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lossiemouth is a fishing town and harbour on the Moray coast of north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Vehicle almost failing to operate

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a machine that is bust has broken down

explanation.surface: A vehicle that has very nearly broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Novelist concealing disgusted expression in polite greeting to woman

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the greeting wraps round the exclamation

parts.note: ma'am is a respectful form of address to a woman
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A writer hides his distaste behind a courteous hello to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: MA'AM drops its apostrophe in the grid, as crosswords ignore punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Somerset Maugham wrote Of Human Bondage and The Moon and Sixpence.

clue.text: Unidentified person, rather overlooking rule, embracing the writer

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside
overlooking means leaving out, so the letter for rule is dropped

parts.note: 'I'd rather' and 'I'd sooner' mean the same
the writer of the clue refers to herself or himself as me

explanation.surface: An anonymous figure who preferred to ignore the rules and hug the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' removes R from SOONER, leaving SOONE; 'embracing' then wraps it round the writer, so the setter speaks as 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone means a person not named or known, an anonymous individual.

clue.text: A sauce spoon needs treatment — such as washing-up liquid?

definitions.note: an adjective; the question mark marks the liquid as an example of a soapy thing

indicators.note: something needing treatment is to be worked on and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spoon covered in sauce needs cleaning, perhaps with dish soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Saponaceous is a formal word for soapy, the quality of detergent for dishes.

clue.text: Pain has one going round hospital

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the hospital letter sits inside

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone in pain is wheeled around a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Italian holiday island company adopting Channel Islands? It's light-hearted stuff

parts.note: Capri is an island resort in the Bay of Naples

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the company holds the islands

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, the British islands off Normandy such as Jersey and Guernsey

explanation.surface: A firm on Capri takes over Jersey and Guernsey too and calls it a lark.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, free-form piece of music or art, playful in character.

clue.text: Pig-like monster goring tree

indicators.note: goring means piercing, so the monster pierces into the tree

parts.note: a pine is a tree
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A pig-like monster drives its tusks into a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcine comes from Latin porcus, so it describes things resembling swine.

clue.text: I will avoid obscure part of the world for Disney film

indicators.note: will avoid means the letter keeps out, so it is removed

parts.note: faint and obscure both mean hard to see clearly
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: Someone vows to steer clear of a remote region and watch a cartoon instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will avoid' takes I out of FAINT, leaving FANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 animated feature from the Walt Disney studio set to classical music.

clue.text: Certain to tuck into alcohol in a responsible manner?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective; the question mark admits it describes how one acts

indicators.note: to tuck into means to go inside, so certain is placed within the drink

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink of fermented honey
certain and sure both mean confident

explanation.surface: Someone sure of themselves gets stuck into the drink, but sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured behaviour is careful and restrained, the way a responsible person acts.

clue.text: Very old when set beside the old

parts.note: T' is an old dialect form of the

indicators.note: old set beside its own copy is doubled

explanation.surface: Something deemed elderly when placed next to the ancients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when set beside' doubles O to OO, which follows T'.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means excessively, as in too hot, a sense close to very.

clue.text: Help and aid distributed for London theatre

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Assistance is handed out to keep a West End playhouse going.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adelphi is a West End playhouse on the Strand.

clue.text: Not initially full, not initially empty

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken
not initially means without its first letter

explanation.surface: A paradox about a vessel that is neither full nor empty to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Null means void, containing nothing at all.

clue.text: Solemn over adolescent getting hooch

parts.note: po is short for po-faced, meaning solemn and humourless
a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: A stern parent watches over a teenager who has got hold of illicit liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is illicit Irish whiskey, a homemade bootleg spirit.

clue.text: Mathematical item: arts graduate gets confused on the radio

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts

indicators.note: heard on the radio means a word with the same sound

parts.note: the graduate gets tricks, deceptions that leave someone confused

explanation.surface: A humanities graduate is baffled by a sum on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a matrix is a rectangular array of numbers treated as a single object.

clue.text: Gutted the insect's weapon, dealing with bugs?

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: a bee or wasp attacks with a sting

explanation.surface: Someone devastated by being stung while working with insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugs' suggests insects, but here they are software faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing software means hunting down faults in the code, so it deals with programming errors.

clue.text: Film director not too keen about very quiet acting

indicators.note: about means around, so the cool word goes round the quiet letters

parts.note: cool means unenthusiastic
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: A film director is unimpressed by understated performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Ford Coppola directed The Godfather and Apocalypse Now.

clue.text: Food that may be listed anywhere except the start of the dictionary?

parts.words: that may be listed anywhere except
parts.note: anything listed anywhere other than the very beginning comes after, or beyond, that point
a dictionary opens with the words under the letter A

explanation.surface: A foodstuff that could be entered on any page of a dictionary but the first ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: the dish is 'past A', so alphabetically it is listed anywhere beyond the opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and other Italian dough products make a staple food.

clue.text: Man needing time to leave prison

indicators.note: to leave means to go out, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A man needs to do his time before getting out of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is a respectful form of address for a man.

clue.text: Epicure curses onion in the soup

indicators.note: in the soup means in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gourmet swears on finding an onion in his soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like where the onion lies, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur is an expert judge of taste, especially in food and wine, like a gourmet.

clue.text: Love letter, unfinished, turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters read from the bottom
unfinished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: to drop someone a line is to send a short letter

explanation.surface: A love letter, never completed, suddenly reappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' trims LINE to LIN; 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis love is a score of zero.

clue.text: Hero of Shaw play with parts including leader of Christians

parts.note: and and with both mean together

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the parts surround the leader

parts.note: actors play parts or roles

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cast of actors in a Shaw play including a Christian leader.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw's Androcles and the Lion is about a Christian who befriends a lion.

clue.text: Article subsequently cut to form additional item

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: next and subsequently both mean afterwards

explanation.surface: A piece of writing is later trimmed to make an addendum.
explanation.definitionFit: An annex is a supplement added to a document, or an extension to a building.
